title: Integral-domain factorization of a finite map at a domain source stalk
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $x\in X$ have a domain local ring $T=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ (a nonzero commutative ring with no zero divisors). Put $R=\mathcal O_{Y,f(x)}$. There exist a commutative domain $B$ and ring homomorphisms $a:R\to B$, $b:B\to T$ such that every element of $B$ is integral over $R$ via $a$, the map $b$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and $b\circ a=f_x^\sharp$. No target normality, Noetherianity or dominance is assumed.

source.place: new-finite-normal-dense-etale-stalk-going-down, steps 1 and 3 (affine integral algebra and stalk localization); Mathlib/RingTheory/Localization/Integral.lean:205 and Mathlib/RingTheory/Unramified/Finite.lean:275 (Iversen I.2.7).

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood U=Spec A of f(x), with finite affine preimage Spec C. Its map A -> C is finite by the definition of finite morphism, and hence integral by the finite-algebra integrality lemma. Write p for f(x), q for x, R=A_p and T=C_q using the affine stalk localization instances.

Let M be the image in C of A minus p, and S=M^{-1}C. The localization of A -> C gives a0:R -> S, integral by Mathlib isIntegral_localization. Elements of M become units in T: map the units of R along f.stalkMap x and use germ_stalkMap_apply. IsLocalization.lift therefore constructs b0:S -> T.

The affine stalk localization makes T flat over C. Since S is a localization of C, Module.flat_iff_of_isLocalization makes T flat over S. IsLocalization.ringHom_ext reduces b0.comp a0 = f.stalkMap x to its equality on A. IsLocalization.map_eq and lift_eq reduce that equality to germ_stalkMap_apply.

Take B to be the image subring of b0 in the domain T, so B is a domain. Let a be a0 followed by the range restriction, and b be the inclusion in T. Every element of B has a preimage in S. Mapping its monic integral equation by RingHom.IsIntegralElem.map proves a.IsIntegral.

The range restriction S -> B is surjective, hence formally unramified and finite as an S-module. Apply the proved Mathlib theorem Algebra.FormallyUnramified.flat_of_restrictScalars (Unramified/Finite.lean:275, Iversen I.2.7) to the tower S -> B -> T, using T flat over S. It proves b.Flat. The range inclusion composed with range restriction is b0, so the required composite equality follows from the equality already proved.

mathlib_searches.query: An integral domain stalk of a finite scheme morphism factors through an integral domain algebra and a flat map
A finite map with normal source has a stalk map factoring through an integral domain algebra followed by a localization
mathlib_searches.results: LocallyOfFiniteType.stalkMap, local stalk homomorphism and HasRingHomProperty results; no factorization theorem.

The search found IsLocalization.isIntegral_localization. Direct source reads found Algebra.FormallyUnramified.flat_of_restrictScalars and affine stalk localizations. Library and blueprint searches found no matching factorization declaration.

lean.statement:
theorem finite_stalk_integral_domain_factorization {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite f] (x : X) (hX : IsDomain (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    ∃ (B : CommRingCat.{u}) (a : Y.presheaf.stalk (f x) →+* B)
      (b : B →+* X.presheaf.stalk x),
      IsDomain B ∧ a.IsIntegral ∧ b.Flat ∧ b.comp a = (f.stalkMap x).hom
